content: We have mass spec: m/z 193.1103 (most intense). Likely molecular ion M+ at 193.1103. Proton NMR shows signals: 1.20 (d, 3H) suggests ethyl CH3 attached to CH (maybe CH-CH3). 2.85 (d, 2H) suggests CH2 next to something electronegative. 3.09 (qdd, 1H) suggests CH attached to CH3 and CH2? 3.81 (s, 3H) methoxy. Aromatic: 7.15 (ddd, 2H) and 7.92 (ddd, 2H) suggests para-disubstituted aromatic? Actually pattern of 2,2 aromatic maybe 1,4-disubstituted gives AA'BB' doublets. But here ddd suggests ortho meta etc maybe 1,2,4-trisubstituted? Two sets of 2H each suggests symmetrical? Could be anisole (methoxy phenyl) with para substituent? The aromatic signals: 7.15 (ddd) 2H, 7.92 (ddd) 2H. That could be para-disubstituted phenyl with electron-withdrawing group causing downfield shift for ortho protons. The methoxy at 3.81 suggests anisole. So likely anisole ring with para carbonyl side chain? The side chain: C(=O)C(C)CN suggests an amide? Actually COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)C(C)CN: that's anisoyl (p-methoxybenzoyl) attached to alpha carbon bearing methyl and CH2NH? Wait structure: anisole ring attached to carbonyl (C=O) attached to C(C)CN (alpha carbon with methyl and CH2NH). That gives CH (1H) at 3.09 (qdd) attached to CH3 (1.20 d) and CH2 (2.85 d). CH2 attached to N (maybe primary amine). The mass: Let's compute formula for that SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)C(C)CN. Use get_formula.
